question_en: What is the timeline for expedited reporting of fatal or life-threatening unexpected ADRs?
question_es: ¿Cuál es el plazo de notificación expeditiva de una reacción adversa inesperada mortal o potencialmente mortal?
notes: ICH E2A §III.B.1 (p.7): notify as soon as possible, no later than 7 calendar days after first knowledge; complete report within 8 additional calendar days.

question_en: How many days does the sponsor have to report a serious unexpected ADR that is not fatal or life-threatening?
question_es: ¿Cuántos días tiene el promotor para notificar una reacción adversa grave e inesperada que no sea mortal ni potencialmente mortal?
notes: ICH E2A §III.B.2 (p.7): as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days after first knowledge that the case meets the minimum criteria.

question_en: How does ICH E2A define a serious adverse event or reaction?
question_es: ¿Cómo define ICH E2A un acontecimiento adverso grave?
notes: ICH E2A §II.B (p.5): any untoward medical occurrence that at any dose results in death, is life-threatening, requires inpatient hospitalisation or prolongation, results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity, or is a congenital anomaly/birth defect. Note: 'life-threatening' = at risk of death at the time of the event.

question_en: When is an adverse drug reaction considered 'unexpected' under ICH E2A?
question_es: ¿Cuándo se considera 'inesperada' una reacción adversa según ICH E2A?
notes: ICH E2A §II.A.3 (p.4): nature or severity not consistent with the applicable product information (e.g. the Investigator's Brochure for an unapproved IMP).

question_en: What are the minimum criteria a case must meet before an expedited initial report is submitted?
question_es: ¿Qué criterios mínimos debe cumplir un caso para enviar la notificación expeditiva inicial?
notes: ICH E2A §III.C (p.8): an identifiable patient, a suspect medicinal product, an identifiable reporting source (and an event/outcome identified as serious and unexpected with reasonable suspected causal relationship, p.11).

question_en: Which elements must the informed consent discussion and form cover according to ICH E6(R3)?
question_es: ¿Qué elementos deben cubrir la discusión y el formulario de consentimiento informado según ICH E6(R3)?
notes: ICH E6(R3) §2.8.10 (pp.24-25): list (a)-(r): purpose, research nature, IMP and randomisation probability, procedures, participant responsibilities, foreseeable risks, expected benefits, alternatives, compensation, payment, voluntary participation, data handling, contacts, etc.

question_en: What must happen when a participant or their legally acceptable representative cannot read the informed consent form?
question_es: ¿Qué debe ocurrir cuando el participante o su representante legal no sabe leer el formulario de consentimiento informado?
notes: ICH E6(R3) §2.8.9 (p.24): an impartial witness present (remotely or in person) during the entire discussion; form read and explained; oral consent; witness signs. Glossary 'Impartial Witness' (Appendix C.3.3, p.81).

question_en: What does ICH E6(R3) say about consent in emergency situations where it cannot be obtained before trial participation?
question_es: ¿Qué dice ICH E6(R3) sobre el consentimiento en situaciones de emergencia en las que no puede obtenerse antes de la participación?
notes: ICH E6(R3) Principle 2.4 (p.11): consent obtained from the participant or their legally acceptable representative as soon as possible, in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements and IRB/IEC approval.

question_en: Under ICH E6(R3), what must the investigator do when a serious adverse event occurs?
question_es: Según ICH E6(R3), ¿qué debe hacer el investigador cuando ocurre un acontecimiento adverso grave?
notes: ICH E6(R3) §2.7.2 (p.22): report all SAEs immediately to the sponsor (after reasonably becoming aware), with an assessment of causality, except those the protocol identifies as not needing immediate reporting; follow-up reports as necessary.

question_en: What are the sponsor's obligations regarding SUSARs under ICH E6(R3)?
question_es: ¿Qué obligaciones tiene el promotor respecto a las SUSAR según ICH E6(R3)?
notes: ICH E6(R3) §3.13.2 (p.43): expedite reporting of all SUSARs to regulatory authorities per applicable requirements and ICH E2A; report SUSARs to investigators/institutions and IRB/IEC in a manner reflecting urgency. IRB/IEC also receives SUSARs (§1.4.8).

question_en: What is the Investigator's Brochure and what is its purpose?
question_es: ¿Qué es el manual del investigador (Investigator's Brochure) y para qué sirve?
notes: ICH E6(R3) Appendix A.1 (p.59): a compilation of the clinical and nonclinical data on the IMP relevant to its study in human participants; provides investigators with information to support compliance with the protocol and a risk-benefit assessment. Sponsor keeps it up to date (A.1.1, 3.15.1).

question_en: For how long and by whom must essential records be retained according to ICH E6(R3)?
question_es: ¿Durante cuánto tiempo y quién debe conservar los documentos esenciales según ICH E6(R3)?
notes: ICH E6(R3) Principle 9.5 (p.13) and §2.12.12 (p.30): retained securely by sponsors and investigators for the required period per applicable regulatory requirements, or until the sponsor informs the investigator they are no longer needed; available to regulators, monitors, auditors, IRB/IEC.

question_en: What does the Declaration of Helsinki say about research with participants who cannot give consent?
question_es: ¿Qué dice la Declaración de Helsinki sobre la investigación con participantes que no pueden dar su consentimiento?
notes: Helsinki 2024 ¶28-30: consent from the legally authorized representative considering the participant's preferences; only if the research is likely to benefit them personally or entails minimal risk and burden; assent sought when possible, dissent respected (¶29); ¶30 covers research in conditions preventing consent.

question_en: Under what circumstances does the Declaration of Helsinki allow the use of placebo?
question_es: ¿En qué circunstancias permite la Declaración de Helsinki el uso de placebo?
notes: Helsinki 2024 ¶33: benefits/risks of a new intervention tested against the best proven one(s), except where no proven intervention exists, or where compelling and scientifically sound methodological reasons require placebo/no intervention and participants will not be subject to additional risks of serious or irreversible harm.

question_en: What post-trial provisions does the Declaration of Helsinki require?
question_es: ¿Qué disposiciones posteriores al ensayo exige la Declaración de Helsinki?
notes: Helsinki 2024 ¶34: in advance of a clinical trial, sponsors and researchers must arrange post-trial provisions for all participants who still need an intervention identified as beneficial; the protocol must describe them (¶22).

question_en: Does the Declaration of Helsinki require trials to be registered?
question_es: ¿Exige la Declaración de Helsinki registrar los ensayos?
notes: Helsinki 2024 ¶35: research involving human participants must be registered in a publicly accessible database before recruitment of the first participant.

question_en: Compare what ICH E6(R3) and the Declaration of Helsinki require when enrolling participants who are not capable of giving informed consent themselves.
question_es: Compara lo que exigen ICH E6(R3) y la Declaración de Helsinki al incluir participantes que no pueden dar su consentimiento informado por sí mismos.
notes: Multi-source: E6(R3) §2.8.13 / 2.4 (legally acceptable representative, participant informed per understanding) vs Helsinki ¶28-30 (legally authorized representative, benefit or minimal risk, assent/dissent). Both documents must be retrieved and attributed separately.

question_es: ¿Qué fármaco GLP-1 es mejor para perder peso?

question_en: What does 21 CFR Part 50 say about informed consent?
question_es: ¿Qué dice el 21 CFR Part 50 sobre el consentimiento informado?
notes: FDA regulation not indexed. Retrieval is grounded (consent passages score ~0.77), so the gate does not refuse; the answer must state that 21 CFR is not in the knowledge base rather than invent FDA content.

question_en: What does the EU Clinical Trials Regulation 536/2014 say about the timelines for SUSAR reporting to EudraVigilance?
question_es: ¿Qué dice el Reglamento (UE) 536/2014 sobre los plazos de notificación de SUSAR a EudraVigilance?
notes: EU CTR is not indexed; E2A timelines will be retrieved. The answer must not attribute them to Regulation 536/2014 or Article 42; it should say the regulation is not in its sources.

question_en: What does ICH E6(R3) require when reported trial data are changed or corrected?
question_es: ¿Qué exige ICH E6(R3) cuando se modifican o corrigen datos del ensayo ya registrados?
notes: ICH E6(R3) §2.12.6 (p.29): changes/corrections traceable, explained if necessary, must not obscure the original entry (audit trail, §2.12.2 p.28). §3.16.1 (p.47-49): sponsor must not change investigator/participant data unless justified and agreed; corrections justified and supported by source records; computerised-system audit trails.

question_en: From the investigator to the regulatory authority: who reports a serious adverse reaction to whom, and within which timelines, according to ICH E6(R3) and ICH E2A?
question_es: Del investigador a la autoridad reguladora: ¿quién notifica una reacción adversa grave a quién y en qué plazos, según ICH E6(R3) e ICH E2A?
notes: Multi-source: investigator -> sponsor immediately with causality (E6(R3) §2.7.2); sponsor -> regulators expedited per E2A (E6(R3) §3.13.2): 7 days fatal/life-threatening + 8 for completion, 15 days other serious unexpected (E2A §III.B); sponsor -> investigators/IRB-IEC with urgency.
